To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the TimeC notation provides a simple and expressive means to specify the time properties of programs; (2) the TimeC specification mechanism is language independent; and, (3) the synthesis of TimeC specifications is always tractable.

1) the TimeC notation is a novel and expressive mechanism for specifying timing properties of real-time programs; 2) TimeC specifications can be instrumented in a non-intrusive manner; 3) the program synthesis problem posed by TimeC specifications is always tractable.

TimeC: (a) is a language-independent, non-intrusive mechanism for specifying timing constraints on programs, (b) yields synthesis questions that are always tractable, and (c) can be used to generate code for microprocessors with ILPs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel language and compiler technology for the assured and efficient compilation of real-time software for microprocessor architectures with ILP.
the development of a language and compiler technology for the assured, rapid prototyping of embedded applications.
the design and implementation of a compiler framework that will support the rapid development of real-time software.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TimeC provides a language for specifying properties of programs that is both tractable and sufficiently expressive to be of use in the context of embedded applications.
TimeC is an effective and tractable notation for specifying timing constraints for programs, independent of their language of origin.
TimeC is the first language for specifying timing properties that is both expressive and tractable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TimeC is an elegant, expressive and tractable language for specifying time properties of embedded programs.
TimeC is a language independent notation for specifying timing properties in programs that is amenable to automated analysis.
TimeC offers an attractive alternative to the extant approaches for specifying timing properties of programs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the synthesis of real-time programs can be made tractable, even when using a general purpose, high-level programming language.
TimeC can be used to develop real-time embedded software in a manner that is both efficient and tractable.
TimeC is a viable mechanism for specifying timing requirements of real-time embedded applications, and that the program synthesis problems that arise out of these specifications are always tractable.
